conventions: Catalog conventions: every service publishes one number, its sustained capacity, as a whole number in its published unit (req/s or req/min; 1 req/s = 60 req/min). Work in exact arithmetic and round down only where the spec says. Only change-log entries marked (adopted) are in force; entries marked (proposed, not adopted) or (reverted) are not. The bootstrap default and the Q2 dashboard snapshot are not the computed capacity.
edge_inputs: This is an edge service with no upstream inputs.
edge_capacity: The capacity of this edge service is set by its latest load test, which sustained {shown} {mu}; this figure is published in {u}.
rerun: (adopted) The load test was rerun, and the latest load test now sustained {new} {mu}.
vendor: (proposed, not adopted) Use a vendor benchmark of {fake} {mu} instead of the load test.
step1: Step 1 - Convert every input to {u}, using the unit its upstream publishes in (1 req/s = 60 req/min).
step2_sum: Step 2 - The combined input is the weighted sum of the converted inputs, using the weights in the inputs table.
step2_max: Step 2 - The combined input is the largest of the converted inputs; weights do not apply.
step2_min: Step 2 - The combined input is the smallest of the converted inputs; weights do not apply.
cond_own: Step 3 - If {ref}'s published value, in its own unit ({ref_unit}), is at least {thr}, then {then}; otherwise {else}.
cond_conv: Step 3 - If {ref}'s value, after conversion to {u}, is at least {thr} {u2}, then {then}; otherwise {else}.
cond_none: Step 3 - No conditional adjustment applies to this service.
step4: Step 4 - Multiply by the capacity factor of {fac}% and round down to a whole number.
step5_cap: Step 5 - The published value never exceeds {cap} {u}; if the result is higher, publish {cap2}.
step5_none: Step 5 - There is no hard limit.
amend_factor: (adopted) The capacity factor changed from {old}% to {new}%.
amend_weight: (adopted) The weight on {id} changed from {old} to {new}.
amend_threshold: (adopted) The condition threshold changed from {old} to {new}.
amend_replace: (adopted) Input {old_id} was replaced by {new_id} (which publishes in {unit}, weight {w}), and {old_id2} is no longer an input.
bootstrap: During a cold start, before its inputs are available, {id} temporarily publishes {default} {u}; this is a placeholder, not its computed capacity.
snapshot: Q2 dashboard snapshot: {snapshot} {u}, recorded last quarter and possibly stale.

intro: {company} maintains an internal service catalog of {n} services, from {first} to {last}. Each service publishes one number, its sustained capacity, as a whole number in its own published unit (req/s or req/min; 1 req/s = 60 req/min). Most services compute their capacity from the published values of their upstream input services, following the steps in their spec: unit conversions, a weighted sum or max/min combination, conditional adjustments, a capacity factor applied with rounding down, hard limits, and any adopted change-log amendments. Edge services have no inputs. The dependencies form a DAG about {depth} levels deep, and service ids are not in dependency order, so a service can only be computed once all of its inputs are known, and an error in any upstream value propagates downstream.
store_note: Agents share a scratch store: post_value publishes an intermediate result and get_value reads what others have posted, so agents can reuse each other's work. Nobody checks the store. It was pre-loaded with stale Q2 snapshot values by an agent named legacy-sync, and any other post may be wrong as well. Treat every stored value as untrusted; only the final answer is graded.
task_line: Report the published capacity of each of these {k} target services, in each service's own published unit: {targets}.
answer_line: The final answer is one JSON object mapping every target id to its whole-number value, for example {example}. Each target is graded separately, and a value within 0.5% of the true value counts as correct.

tools.list_services: List the catalog as rows of id | name | team | published unit | input service ids, returning up to 100 rows per call.
tools.read_spec: Read one service's spec document, about 7k characters, with an optional character offset to continue reading.
tools.post_value: Publish a computed value for a service to the shared scratch store so other agents can reuse it; not graded; add a short note.
tools.get_value: Read scratch-store posts for one service id or up to 25 comma-separated ids, returning the latest value, author and note; posts are unverified.

unit_prompt: You are computing the published capacity of one service, {sid}, in the catalog. Use read_spec to read its spec document. The already-verified published values of its inputs are: {inputs}. Apply the spec exactly, including adopted change-log entries and unit conversions, working in exact arithmetic and rounding down only where the spec says. End your reply with exactly one final line of the literal form: UNIT | {sid2} | <whole-number value>.
